title: zazzle git use cases
description: What a developer does with zazzle git, step by step: write a message as git's editor, commit with a kept draft and chosen files, and reorder or squash commits in an interactive rebase; and how a coding agent commits without the editor.

entities.name: Write a commit message in git's editor
entities.description: A developer who set `zazzle git message` (or git-tools-commit-message-editor) as git's editor writes the message git asks for and saves or cancels.
entities.goal: Write the message in a small editor without modes, with git's comment block kept and the subject length shown, and have git go on or stop.
preconditions: git's core.editor or GIT_EDITOR names `zazzle git message` or git-tools-commit-message-editor.
git runs in a terminal the editor can open as /dev/tty.
postconditions: Saved: the file holds the edited text followed by git's unchanged comment tail, written atomically with its permissions kept, and the exit status is 0, so git goes on.
Cancelled: the file is unchanged and the exit status is 1, so git aborts.

flow.action: Runs a git command that opens the editor, such as git commit, git merge or git tag -a.

Takes the one FILE argument (skipping +LINE and --), reads it, recognises its kind from the name and splits off git's trailing comment block and everything from the scissors line, using git's core.commentChar.
Puts /dev/tty in raw mode on the alternate screen with bracketed paste and the kitty keyboard protocol, and draws the text, the dimmed comment tail, the subject counter and the key bar.
Types the message, moving with arrows and their double and triple taps, and presses Ctrl+S.
Writes the text to a temporary file beside the target, syncs it and renames it over the target, then restores the terminal and exits 0.

alternatives.condition: No FILE, or more than one.
alternatives.outcome: The error and the help on standard error, exit 2.

alternatives.condition: The file is larger than 256 KiB or is not UTF-8.
alternatives.outcome: `... use another editor` on standard error, exit 1; a missing file opens empty.

alternatives.condition: There is no terminal to open.
alternatives.outcome: `needs a terminal: ...` on standard error, exit 1.

alternatives.condition: Ctrl+S on a commit message with only blank and comment lines.
alternatives.outcome: `The message is empty (Esc cancels)` and editing goes on.
With nothing changed it cancels at once; otherwise it asks `Discard your changes? y/n` and y cancels. Cancelling exits 1 without writing.

alternatives.condition: SIGHUP, SIGTERM or SIGINT arrives, or the terminal closes.
alternatives.outcome: Editing ends as cancelled, the terminal is restored, exit 1.

entities.name: Commit with a drafted message and chosen files
entities.description: A developer runs `zazzle git commit` to write the message and choose what each changed file does in this commit, in one screen, without losing the message if the commit fails.
entities.goal: Commit the right files with a well-formed message, keeping the draft and the marks until a commit succeeds.
preconditions: The working directory is inside a git work tree with changes, or --amend is given.
git-tools is installed beside zazzle, or git-tools-commit is run directly, in a terminal.
postconditions: On success: the files are staged, untracked, ignored or deleted as marked, git commit has run with the draft, and the draft and marks files are gone.
On a cancel or a failed commit: the draft stays in the git directory and the next run reopens it; after a failed commit the marks stay too, until HEAD moves.

flow.action: Runs `zazzle git commit` (optionally --no-add and git commit options such as --amend or --signoff).

Moves to the repository root, reads git status with every untracked file, marks changed tracked files [ADD] (only staged ones with --no-add), and applies the saved marks if they were made on the same HEAD.
When there is no draft yet, writes .git/ZAZZLE_COMMIT_MSG from the last message (amend) or commit.template, followed by guidance comments and the branch.
Writes the message, presses Tab for the Files view, marks each file with Space (blank, [ADD], [IGNORE], [REMOVE]), A or Backspace ([DELETE]), and presses Ctrl+S.
Saves the draft and the marks (.git/ZAZZLE_COMMIT_FILES, with HEAD), then deletes, ignores, untracks, adds and unstages files in that order.
Runs `git commit --cleanup=strip -F DRAFT` with the other options, attached to the terminal; on success removes the draft and the marks, and exits with git's status.

alternatives.outcome: No editor: `git commit -a ARGS` (without -a under --no-add) runs at once and its status is returned.

alternatives.condition: Nothing changed and --amend is not given, or a git query fails.
alternatives.outcome: `zazzle git commit: nothing to commit` (or git's error) on standard error, exit 1.
Ctrl+S asks `Delete N file(s) from disk? ... y/n`; only y goes on.
Exit 1; no marks are saved and nothing is staged or committed.

alternatives.condition: A file was staged in a repository with no commits yet and is left out.
alternatives.outcome: It is unstaged with git rm --cached instead of git reset.

alternatives.condition: git commit fails, for example a hook rejects it.
alternatives.outcome: git's exit status is returned and the draft and marks are kept for the next run.

entities.name: Reorder and squash commits in an interactive rebase
entities.description: A developer whose git sequence editor is the zazzle git editor changes the todo list of git rebase -i in the Rebase view.
entities.goal: Set each commit's command and order with single keys, and start or abort the rebase.
preconditions: core.editor, GIT_EDITOR or GIT_SEQUENCE_EDITOR names `zazzle git message` or git-tools-commit-message-editor.
git rebase -i runs in a terminal.
postconditions: Start rebase: git-rebase-todo holds the new commands and order, exit 0, and git carries out the rebase, opening the editor again for each message it asks for.
Abort rebase: the todo list is unchanged, exit 1, and git stops the rebase.

flow.action: Recognises git-rebase-todo, keeps git's comment block read-only and opens in the Rebase view, showing each command's full name; Ctrl+S is labelled Start rebase and Esc Abort rebase.
Moves to a line and presses p, r, e, s, f or d for pick, reword, edit, squash, fixup or drop; Alt+Up/Down moves the line; then Ctrl+S.
Saves the todo list atomically and exits 0.

alternatives.condition: The key is not a command key or the line is not a commit command.
alternatives.outcome: `p r e s f d set the command of a commit line` and nothing changes.

alternatives.condition: Ctrl+S when the first commit that is not dropped is a squash or fixup.
alternatives.outcome: `The first commit cannot be a squash` (or fixup) and editing goes on.

alternatives.condition: Esc (after y to discard, when anything changed).
alternatives.outcome: Exit 1 and git stops the rebase.

entities.name: Commit from a coding agent without the editor
entities.description: A coding agent following the zazzle skill commits with `zazzle git commit -m`, which never opens the terminal editor.
entities.goal: Commit all tracked changes, or only the staged ones, with a given message in one non-interactive command.
preconditions: The agent's working directory is inside a git work tree.
postconditions: git commit has run with the message, and its exit status is the command's.

flow.action: Runs `zazzle git commit -m MSG`, adding --no-add to commit only what is staged.
Sees a message option and runs `git commit -a -m MSG` (without -a under --no-add) attached to the caller's streams, returning git's exit status.

alternatives.condition: Nothing is staged or changed, or a hook rejects the commit.
alternatives.outcome: git's own message and non-zero exit status.
